concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: Torah #101 is a lengthy practical teaching about the centrality of prayer, Psalms, and supplication in the war against the evil inclination. While it uses the phrase 'בְּאֵיזֶה בְּחִינָה שֶׁהוּא' (line 6), this means 'in whatever manner/way' — it is NOT a bechina equation. The teaching contains no explicit bechina (parallel-aspect) statements equating concepts. All relationships are causal/advisory: tikkun chatzot enables pouring out one's heart (eitza); saying Psalms is the foundation for winning the war against the yetzer hara (eitza); persistent prayer leads to closeness to God (eitza). Key concepts: תִּקּוּן חֲצוֹת (Tikkun Chatzot), הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת (hitbodedut), תְּהִלִּים (Psalms), תְּפִלָּה (prayer), מִלְחֲמוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע (wars of the evil inclination), חִזּוּק (strengthening). None are connected via bechina language.
